uncited: **Texture Unit 1 (Scalar Data):** A 2D paletted texture with 8-bit precision storing scalar values.
**Texture Unit 2 (Gradient Directions):** An 8-bit paletted texture storing normalized gradient directions.
**Texture Unit 3 (Gradient Magnitude):** A paletted texture storing gradient magnitudes.
**Texture Unit 4 (Distance/Position):** A 1-D texture storing distance modulation.
*   Setup Texture Unit 2 to modulate the color from Texture Unit 1 (scalar data).
**Opacity Modulation:** Texture Unit 3 (gradient magnitude) modulates the opacity.
**Color Depth Cueing:** Texture Unit 4 (distance modulation) modulates the color.
This pass adds silhouettes and specular highlights.
*   **Silhouette:** Assign palette entries an opacity that is highest when the transformed gradient vector is perpendicular to the viewing direction (dot product near zero).
*   **Specular:** Calculate specular lighting contribution for each encoded gradient direction and add it to the RGB palette entry.
**Silhouette/Specular Modulation:** Texture Unit 3 (gradient magnitude) modulates the silhouette/specular contribution.
**Distance Opacity Modulation:** Texture Unit 4 modulates opacity based on distance.
To render different types of objects simultaneously, the user specifies multiple transfer functions, each with its own set of NPR parameters.

*   **Interactivity vs. Resolution:** Standard techniques of rendering lower resolution data to achieve interactivity are unsuited for non-photorealistic parameter selection because NPR techniques clarify fine structures.
*   **Gradient Enhancement Direction:** Enhancing regions with the highest gradient magnitude emphasizes transitions.
If one wants to visualize structures between two materials of similar scalar value, enhancing high gradient regions would emphasize the wrong features.
*   **Time Complexity:** Two rendering passes per view-aligned polygon.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for four paletted textures per volume (scalar, gradient direction, gradient magnitude, distance).
